claims.text: The target material is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature produce accelerated coupled degradation relative to the baseline.
Dynamic amorphization causes the accelerated coupled degradation.
The dynamic amorphization model accurately predicts grain-size-dependent shear strength in the inverse Hall-Petch regime.
A protective oxide layer forms under the stated elevated-temperature exposure.
Formation of a protective oxide layer increases wear resistance at elevated temperature.
Protective oxide phases can improve corrosion resistance by acting as barriers against further oxidation.
The controlled comparison uses the alloy with and without simultaneous wear and corrosion exposure at elevated temperature.
Wear resistance, corrosion resistance, and microstructure are measured in the proposed experiment.
Failure of the dynamic amorphization model to predict grain-size-dependent shear strength would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of the protective oxide layer to increase wear resistance at elevated temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The protective oxide is treated as increasing wear resistance, while the stated outcome is accelerated total degradation; the hypothesis does not explain how this protective response contributes to, or is overcome in, the accelerated degradation.
The structural mediator is oxide-layer formation, but the named mechanism is dynamic amorphization. No causal relationship between oxide formation and dynamic amorphization is stated.
